result.summary: This pull request backports three merged changes (#36869, #36889, and #36894) to the 31.x release branch and updates the v31.x release notes. In net_processing, it changes peer discouragement to set the disconnect flag on the offending connection rather than disconnecting all connections sharing the IP. It also modernizes CMake include directives to target-based commands and makes STL helper struct fields in memusage public to suppress compiler warnings.
result.problem: When a peer misbehaved, MaybeDiscourageAndDisconnect previously disconnected all connections matching the peer's IP address. For clearnet-over-tor connections, an attacker sharing an exit node's IP could deliberately send invalid messages to disconnect all honest inbound connections using that exit node. In addition, newer toolchains (Clang 24 and CMake 4.5.0) emitted build warnings for unused private fields in memory accounting structs and global include directory directives.
evidence: Commit 35f34a31a6 (#36894): "If a node has an honest clearnet-over-tor inbound connection, the IP of the inbound peer will be the exit node's IP address. If an attacker connects to the node through the same exit node and sends an invalid message, they can cause every inbound peer sharing the exit node's IP to get disconnect."
Commit 72d6048d5f (#36869): "Since llvm/llvm-project#237374, Clang 24 diagnoses these fields with -Wunused-private-field."
Commit c4547c490f (#36889): "As of CMake 4.5.0, it triggers -Wnon-target-directive warnings."
result.scope_notes: Backport bundle targeting the 31.x maintenance branch containing three distinct cherry-picked pull requests (#36869, #36889, #36894) and release notes updates.
result.changed_since_previous: Added backports of #36889 (CMake target_include_directories update) and #36894 (fixing collateral disconnection of shared-IP peers during discouragement) in addition to the original #36869.
result.card: Backports PRs #36869, #36889, and #36894 to the 31.x release branch alongside release note updates. The primary bugfix (#36894) resolves a denial-of-service issue where an attacker sharing a Tor exit node's IP could disconnect honest clearnet-over-tor inbound peers when triggering node discouragement, fixed by disconnecting only the misbehaving node instead of the entire subnet. The PR also suppresses toolchain warnings by making memusage STL struct fields public for Clang 24 and migrating global include directives to target_include_directories for CMake 4.5.0.

risk.why: A regression in peer disconnection handling could allow misbehaving peers to remain connected or inadvertently disconnect honest peers on the network.
